clue.text: Walk from American time and charge into New York time

indicators.note: one thing going into another means it is placed inside it

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for American
an eon is a vast stretch of time
Eastern Standard Time, the clock New York keeps
a fee is a charge for a service

explanation.surface: A traveller crossing from US time zones into New York time, paying a charge along the way.
explanation.walkthrough: The charge sits inside EST, Eastern Standard Time, after US and EON.
explanation.definitionFit: To use one's feet is the idiom for going on foot rather than riding, which is exactly walking.

clue.text: Source of 17 scattered seed of Terah with topping of mulch

indicators.note: seed that is scattered is strewn about, so the letters are thrown into a new order
topping a plant or a person cuts off the head, so the first letter goes

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written; Terah was Abraham's father
mulch with its first letter cut off

explanation.surface: A biblical gardening scene: Terah's seed scattered with a layer of mulch on top.
explanation.walkthrough: 17 is ABRAHAM. Genesis says Terah took his son Abram out of Ur of the Chaldees, so the city is where Abraham came from.
explanation.definitionFit: Genesis names this Mesopotamian city as Abraham's birthplace, the origin from which he set out with his father.

clue.text: Crack up making those absent from W --- K, say?

blocks.note: surface reading: to break down laughing or collapse

blocks.clueFragment: making those absent from W --- K, say?
blocks.note: setter's reading: ex- marks those who are gone, as though the missing letters of a word with gaps had been removed

explanation.surface: Someone cracking up, apparently because letters have gone missing from a word with gaps.
explanation.walkthrough: Crack up here means to praise highly, as in cracking something up to be great; the rest plays on EX as the prefix for those who are no longer present.
explanation.definitionFit: To crack someone up is an idiom for talking them up, praising them highly, which is what extolling means.

clue.text: Name one Greek island: one with a divided capital

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for name
the Roman numeral for one
Cos (Kos) is a Greek island in the Dodecanese
the Roman numeral for one again
taken as written

explanation.surface: A quiz question naming a Greek island, then a city cut in two.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Name one Greek island' looks like a request, but it is just three pieces in a row.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyprus's capital has been split since 1974 by a buffer zone between Greek Cypriot and Turkish Cypriot sectors.

clue.text: Ignore the alarm! These slippery customers are over a barrel

indicators.note: in a down entry, being turned over means the word is read upwards

blocks.note: eels are proverbially slippery
a pin is a small cask holding half a firkin

explanation.surface: A warning about crooks who have someone at their mercy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over a barrel' looks like the idiom for being helpless, but the eels go over a small barrel in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Staying in bed past the usual hour means letting the wake-up signal go unheeded.

clue.text: Labour's injection of backbone?

blocks.note: surface reading: the Labour Party being given some courage
setter's reading: an injection into the spine given during childbirth

explanation.surface: A political jibe that the Labour Party needs stiffening up.
explanation.walkthrough: Labour is childbirth, not the party, and backbone is literal: the spinal anaesthetic.
explanation.definitionFit: This anaesthetic is injected near the spinal cord and is commonly given to women in childbirth to numb pain.

clue.text: Destination of 17's line and then of a canal restoration

indicators.note: restoring something rebuilds it, so the words are reassembled in a fresh order

blocks.note: the fodder, all fifteen letters

explanation.surface: A canal restoration project describing where a line will run.
explanation.walkthrough: 17 is ABRAHAM; his line is his descendants. 'Line' and 'canal' paint waterways, but the definition is biblical.
explanation.definitionFit: The Promised Land given to Abraham's descendants in Genesis was Canaan, so it was where his lineage was headed.

clue.text: "The ______ 16,4,17's 23" (Richard III)

blocks.note: surface reading: a quotation with a gap and cross-references
setter's reading: fill the gap in Tyrrel's line about the murdered princes

explanation.walkthrough: With 16, 4, 17 and 23 filled in, the line reads 'The sons of Edward sleep in Abraham's bosom', said of the princes in the Tower.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing words of Shakespeare's line refer to the two boys, children of King Edward IV, murdered in the Tower.

clue.text: Successful deal maker is caught by failure

indicators.note: one thing set by another simply stands next to it in the light

blocks.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
a loser is one who fails

explanation.surface: A dealmaker brought down by a failure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caught by' suggests a container, but the two pieces just sit side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: In sales jargon a closer is the person brought in to finalise agreements and seal the sale.

clue.text: Spoken verse in instalments through one's teeth!

indicators.note: spoken means we go by how the words are said aloud, not spelt

blocks.note: an ode is a poem; on tick means paid for on credit, bit by bit

explanation.surface: A poem recited in pieces, muttered through gritted teeth.
explanation.walkthrough: On tick is British slang for on credit, paid in instalments.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a dental term from the Greek for tooth, describing what concerns the teeth.

clue.text: English truffle hunter swilling ale close to the ground

indicators.note: swilling sloshes a liquid around, so the letters are swirled into another order

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for English
pigs are traditionally used to sniff out truffles
ale rearranged

explanation.surface: An English truffle-hunting pig drinking beer as it snuffles the soil.
explanation.definitionFit: A botanical term for things growing or living on or just above the soil surface.

clue.text: How an alpine colonist squares accounts?

definitions.note: a cryptic description of what a mountain settler does

blocks.note: first meaning: a colonist in the Alps makes a home high up
second meaning: pays what is owed

explanation.surface: A mountain settler balancing the books.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means paying off a debt or bill so nothing more is owed between parties.

clue.text: 'eaves one within range

indicators.note: within means placed inside the other piece

blocks.note: heaves means hurls; the apostrophe drops the initial H, Cockney style
a means one

explanation.surface: A Cockney straining to lift a cooker range.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'eaves tells you the H has gone, so the synonym loses its H too.
explanation.definitionFit: The mountain chain dividing Europe from Asia in Russia is an example of a mountain range.

clue.text: Contract in Franco-Roman law

blocks.note: Franco- is the prefix for French, abbreviated F
lex is the Latin word for law

explanation.surface: A legal agreement drawn up under Franco-Roman law.
explanation.walkthrough: Contract looks like a legal noun but is the verb, as muscles tighten.
explanation.definitionFit: Flexing a muscle tightens and bunches it, which is the sense of the verb contract.

clue.text: As man involved with Ireland might view one from England

indicators.note: involved means twisted up together, so the letters are tangled into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: How an Irishman might regard an English visitor.
explanation.definitionFit: Seen from an island, someone from the larger landmass of Great Britain comes from the mainland.

clue.text: Spontaneous declaration: "Release the Stratford One!"

blocks.note: to release is to set free
William Shakespeare, born in Stratford-upon-Avon

explanation.surface: A campaign slogan demanding the release of Shakespeare.
explanation.definitionFit: A free-will offering is given voluntarily, without compulsion, so the adjective means done of one's own accord.

clue.text: So Wordsworth's minstrel appears to have thee flustered, as a matter of fact

indicators.note: someone flustered is in a muddle, so the letters get muddled

blocks.note: thee rearranged
really means in fact

explanation.surface: A poet's minstrel appearing to have unsettled the person addressed.
explanation.walkthrough: Wordsworth's poem To a Skylark opens 'Ethereal minstrel! pilgrim of the sky!'
explanation.definitionFit: Wordsworth called the skylark an airy, heavenly minstrel, so it appears in that light and delicate manner.

clue.text: One of eight from a demoralised War Department

indicators.note: taken from means lifted out of the run of letters that follows

blocks.note: the last two letters of the first word, the whole second word and the first letter of the third

explanation.surface: A king emerging from a War Office whose staff have lost heart.
explanation.walkthrough: England has had eight kings of this name, Edward I to Edward VIII. The 'a' just helps the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Eight English monarchs since the Conquest have borne this name, so any one is one of the eight.

clue.text: Race starter - for the Lincoln!

blocks.note: first meaning: the patriarch who founded the Hebrew people
second meaning: the first name of President Lincoln

explanation.surface: A racecourse starter for the Lincoln, a famous English flat handicap.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lincoln is a horse race that opens the British flat season, so the surface is all about racing.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical patriarch is the father of the Hebrew nation, and the sixteenth US president bore the same given name.

clue.text: One is spotted by Lampedusa

blocks.note: first meaning: a big cat with a spotted coat
second meaning: Lampedusa's novel Il Gattopardo

explanation.surface: Someone sighted near the Italian island of Lampedusa.
explanation.walkthrough: Lampedusa looks like the island but is the Sicilian novelist Giuseppe Tomasi di Lampedusa.
explanation.definitionFit: The big cat has a rosette-spotted coat, and the Sicilian prince's one novel is titled after it in English.

clue.text: Rastafarian held at more than arm's length

indicators.note: held means kept inside the neighbouring word

blocks.note: letters three to six of the word

explanation.surface: A Rastafarian kept at a distance.
explanation.definitionFit: Something beyond reach is some way off, at a distance from where one stands.

clue.text: Shipping line director

blocks.note: surface reading: an executive of a shipping company
setter's reading: the part of a ship that steers its course

explanation.walkthrough: A director sounds like a board member, but it is something that directs a vessel's line of travel.
explanation.definitionFit: The hinged blade at the stern of a vessel turns to steer it along its course.

clue.text: Montcalm's conqueror's in misery about his left foot

indicators.note: about means surrounding the other pieces

blocks.note: woe is misery
standard abbreviation for left
standard abbreviation for foot

explanation.surface: A general in pain about his left foot.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after conqueror stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The British general James Wolfe defeated the French commander Montcalm at Quebec in 1759; both died there.

clue.text: Slater's demand for full pension?

blocks.note: surface reading: a roofer asking for a hotel's full-board terms
setter's reading: the timber a slater needs to lay slates on

explanation.walkthrough: Full pension is hotel-speak for full board; a slater would ask for roof and board rather than room and board.
explanation.definitionFit: These planks are fixed across rafters as a base on which slates or tiles are laid.

clue.text: It could be uplifted for Dr Mowlem to cry on

definitions.note: the subject of the whole clue

indicators.note: lifted up in a down entry means the letters read from bottom to top

blocks.note: Dr Mo Mowlam, Northern Ireland Secretary, known as Mo
to sob is to cry

explanation.surface: Something lifted up for a politician to weep upon.
explanation.walkthrough: Mo Mowlam was a British Labour politician; 'on' puts her name above the cry before both flip upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: One cries on a friend's chest, and a bra uplifts it, so the breast is what the clue describes.

clue.text: His 'n' her venture in hock

indicators.note: to venture is to strike out somewhere new, so the letters move into new places

blocks.note: the 'n' gives N

explanation.surface: A couple's joint venture that has left them in debt.
explanation.walkthrough: In hock looks like the idiom for pawned or in debt; hock is the British name for white wine from the Rhine.
explanation.definitionFit: Hock is German white wine from the Rhine region, and Rhenish is the older name for such wine.

clue.text: Comfort needed when you and me revoltingly grow old

indicators.note: revolting means turning over, so the word is turned back to front

blocks.note: as means when, as in 'as I left'
us is you and me
to age is to grow old

explanation.surface: A wry plea for consolation as a couple ages disgracefully.
explanation.walkthrough: Revoltingly looks like disgust, but it is revolt as in turn over.
explanation.definitionFit: To assuage is to soothe or relieve pain or grief, the verb sense of comfort.

clue.text: Autodidact displaying fame 'n' medals

indicators.note: displaying lays things out afresh, so the letters are set out in a new arrangement

blocks.note: the 'n' gives N

explanation.surface: A self-taught achiever showing off fame and medals.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who rose by their own efforts without help is akin to one who taught themselves without teachers.
